title: Add a batch/bulk insert path and use it in seed_corpus.py
summary: seed_corpus.py inserts one row at a time via store.facts.create() at ~54 rows/sec — seeding the Tier 3 job's 500k-row corpus alone takes ~2.6 hours, already longer than the job's 120-minute timeout, before any actual benchmark step runs.
description:
`benchmarks/seed_corpus.py` (lines 255-290) seeds the corpus with a plain Python `for row_index in range(start_index, total_rows):` loop that calls `store.facts.create(SemanticFact(...), scope)` once per row — a single-row `INSERT` (plus per-checkpoint `commit()`) for every one of the 500,000 rows. `src/agent_memory_sdk/repositories/facts.py` has no bulk/`create_many`/`executemany` method to call instead; every write repository in `src/agent_memory_sdk/repositories/` is single-row only.

The observed Tier 3 run (https://github.com/priyanshu-krishnan1/yaadien/actions/runs/31242532940/job/93077463439, step "Seed 500k corpus (tenant prefix bench)") gives the real throughput directly from its own progress log: 500 rows every ~9.3s and climbing roughly linearly (500 rows @ 8.7s, 1,000 @ 17.5s, ... 17,500 @ 320.7s) — **~54 rows/second**. At that rate, 500,000 rows takes **~2.57 hours**, which alone exceeds the job's `timeout-minutes: 120` (line ~533). The job has never gotten past the seed step in this configuration; it times out and is force-cancelled every run, before "Run full benchmark matrix at 500k rows", "Locust scale ramp (BM-14) — 200 VUs, 15 min", or "Deterministic IR metrics at scale" ever execute.

This is very likely compounded by the already-known, documented Db2 workaround in `repositories/base.py` (~lines 46-60) where vectors can't be bound as parameters (`SQL0901N`) and are instead inlined as SQL string literals via `CAST('{vec}' AS VECTOR(...))` — every INSERT statement ends up textually unique, so Db2 can't reuse a cached access plan across rows the way a parameterized batch/`executemany` could. Coordinate with whoever picks up FLEX-1 (EPIC-25, the seam-extraction story for this same workaround) since a batch-insert design needs to account for the same literal-inlining constraint, not design around bound params that don't actually work on this Db2 version.

Work:
1. Add a batch-insert path to the relevant write repository/repositories (starting with `facts.py`'s `SemanticFact` create path, since that's what `seed_corpus.py` uses) — a multi-row `INSERT ... VALUES (...), (...), ...` or `executemany`-style batch, compatible with the existing vector-literal-inlining constraint.
2. Update `seed_corpus.py` to accumulate rows into batches (e.g. matching or dividing evenly into the existing `_CHECKPOINT_BATCH` checkpoint interval) and call the new batch method instead of one `create()` per row.
3. Benchmark the new path locally against a Db2 container: target at least a 10x throughput improvement (ideally enough to bring 500k-row seeding under 20-30 minutes, leaving real time in Tier 3's budget for the actual benchmark/Locust/IR steps).

Acceptance: `seed_corpus.py --size 50000 ...` (a size that already runs in CI's Tier 2 job) completes measurably faster than before with identical row content/embeddings for the same `--seed`; a local or CI dry-run of `--size 500000` completes seeding well within a fraction of Tier 3's timeout budget, verified via the script's own progress log.
